subject: Accountancy
central_question: How are a partnership firm’s assets realised, liabilities settled and partners’ final claims closed when the business is dissolved?
in_scope_units: Difference between dissolution of partnership and dissolution of the partnership firm.
Modes of dissolution by agreement, compulsory dissolution, contingencies, notice and court order.
Settlement of accounts under Section 48 and application of firm and private property.
Preparation of the Realisation Account and transfer of assets and outside liabilities.
Accounting for asset sales, assets or liabilities taken over by partners and creditors accepting assets.
Realisation expenses, partner remuneration, unrecorded assets and unrecorded liabilities.
Transfer of realisation profit or loss, reserves, fictitious assets, partner loans and final capital balances.
Closure of the Bank Account and the books of the dissolved firm.
banned_topics: Revaluation while a firm continues, which belongs to admission or retirement.
Admission, retirement and death where the business is not closed.
Insolvency of partners and Garner v. Murray beyond the treatment expressly retained in this chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every change in partners dissolves the partnership firm and closes the business.
known_pitfalls.correction: A partnership may dissolve and be reconstituted without dissolution of the firm; dissolution of the firm closes the business and economic relations among all partners.

known_pitfalls.claim: Cash, bank and fictitious assets are transferred to Realisation Account with the other assets.
known_pitfalls.correction: Cash and bank are used for settlement, while fictitious assets are transferred to partners’ capital accounts, not to Realisation Account.

known_pitfalls.claim: Partners’ capital is paid before outside creditors.
known_pitfalls.correction: Outside liabilities are settled first, then partner loans, and only thereafter partners’ capital balances.

known_pitfalls.claim: An unrecorded asset realised has no accounting entry.
known_pitfalls.correction: Bank or the taking-over partner is debited and Realisation Account is credited because the receipt creates a realisation gain.

recommended_example_progression: Use the distinction and modes in Sections 4.1–4.2 with the chapter’s conceptual questions.
